summary.headline: Mold-Tek Q1 FY27 profit rose about 12x YoY with EBITDA margin near 19-23%, though Beryl (US) still contributes nothing to bottom line.
summary.overview: Management said Q1 FY27 profitability was roughly 4x Q4 and 12x Q1 last year, driven by MES downsizing, lower other expenses (including absence of prior-quarter MTM losses) and automation. Beryl, the US residential permitting acquisition, was around break-even and is guided to break even in Q2 and contribute positively from Q3. Civil and structural work on hand was about $4.5 million versus $3.5-3.7 million a year earlier, and MES work on hand was about $1.15 million. Management reiterated FY27 ex-Beryl revenue of Rs 240-250 crore (about Rs 61 crore achieved in Q1) and an indicative Rs 300-350 crore for FY28 together with a structural engineering acquisition.

financial_highlights.change: vs ~15% guided earlier; FY26 EBITDA margin ~11% per management

financial_highlights.metric: Q1 FY27 profit vs prior year
financial_highlights.value: ~12x Q1 FY26 (Q1 FY26 PAT Rs 78 lakh)

financial_highlights.change: vs MTM loss in prior quarter
MES profitable only in FY22-23 and part of FY24 per management

segments.name: Civil & Structural (Mold-Tek Inc.)
segments.commentary: Work on hand about $4.5 million vs $3.5-3.7 million a year ago; project sizes $20k-$500k, lasting 3-12 months. Management treats work on hand as the key leading indicator.

segments.name: MES (Mechanical, Electrical, Structural)
segments.commentary: Work on hand about $1.15 million, flat YoY. Team cut from 125-130 to 50-60 people; EV/automobile design kept at small scale. Power T&D and substation design (poles, towers) now the focus, with a new US power distribution contract (~$1 million per annum, team ramping to 20 by Oct-Nov).

segments.name: Beryl (US residential permitting, Florida; Georgia entry)
segments.commentary: Not yet contributing to bottom line; around break-even, with a marginal loss of $5-10k over 8 months post-acquisition. Received a ~$1 million master purchase order from Hillsborough County; Georgia (Atlanta) listing started.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue ex-Beryl of Rs 240-250 crore reiterated; management says similar Q2 run-rate supports this.
EBITDA margin expected to stay at least 20%, possibly 20-23%, for the current year (management's wording); PAT margin target 15-16% with Beryl adding upside.
Beryl expected to break even in Q2 FY27 and be profitable quarter-on-quarter from Q3-Q4; FY27 Beryl revenue ~$5.5 million at ~8% EBITDA margin; Beryl ceiling ~10% PAT.
FY28 indicative target Rs 300-350 crore, contingent on a structural engineering acquisition.
US data-center-linked power T&D opportunity sized at $5-10 million per annum for Mold-Tek; sector ~$0.5-1 billion.
capex_capacity: MES team cut to 50-60 people from 125-130 a year ago; doubling the power/T&D design team in the last couple of months.
Indian design team for Beryl being built (6-8 people, target 15-20 by Oct-Nov); one PE relocating to Florida from October subject to L1 visa.

Proposed acquisition of a US structural engineering firm (~15 engineers, half PEs/SEs); talks ongoing, CEO to visit US from 16 Aug, chairman late September; decision targeted October and closing possibly within calendar 2026.
Atlanta office (5-6 staff) supports Beryl's Georgia entry; Beryl previously had 38 people at acquisition, lost 2 design staff.
demand_pricing: Civil work on hand $4.5 million (vs $3.7 million last year per one answer; $3.5 million per another), with both existing and new clients.
Power/T&D: new MSA with a US power distribution client; ~10 people billed from July, 20 by Oct-Nov.
Management says Indian rates are very low versus US; focus remains on US work.
Consulting fee model: management aims to charge 2-3% of project cost (vs hourly) once a design firm is integrated.

Beryl's residential/government revenue hit by US government funding shutdown in Jan-May; Florida residential permits reportedly down ~10% YoY (raised by analyst, management attributed partly to demand).

qa_highlights.question: What was the EBITDA per barrel in Q1 and what cost savings are sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Beryl was about break-even; per-barrel EBITDA not given. Savings came from MES downsizing, cut software costs and absence of prior-quarter MTM losses; management called automation and incentive changes long-term.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margin jump to 19% versus 15% guidance and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited reduced automobile engineering costs, automation and productivity incentives visible for 3-5 months, and a work-on-hand build; described these as long-term, not one-time.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Beryl promoter subscribe to warrants?
qa_highlights.answer: The 6-month window lapsed in April when the 6-month average price (~Rs 165) exceeded market (~Rs 130); promoter did not subscribe and management will not press.

qa_highlights.question: Is the $5-10 million power opportunity sector-wide or company-specific?
qa_highlights.answer: Company-specific opportunity of $5-10 million per annum; sector is ~$0.5-1 billion, with ~$100 million of substation design and detailing outsourced from US.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY28 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Indicative Rs 300-350 crore target for FY28 along with a structural engineering acquisition; management said it cannot predict beyond that.

qa_highlights.question: What caused Beryl's sales slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Partly demand (US government funding shutdown for 4-5 months, affecting government-funded work Jan-May) and partly internal design team disruption after losing 2 design staff in November.

risks_watch: Beryl break-even in Q2 and profitability from Q3 depends on building the India design team; cost arbitrage only after Indian staff start executing.
Structural engineering acquisition not yet identified in terms of size or price; timing repeatedly slipped and could fail (management: 'may either take the deal or drop the deal in October').
Revenue and margin guidance is loosely stated; Q1 EBITDA figure (19% vs 23%) and FY26 margin (11% vs 16%) given inconsistently in the call.
MES EV business remains uncertain; management kept a small team hoping for EV revival in 2-3 years.
Work on hand disclosed as a single number; Beryl's work on hand not tracked; US permitting demand and government funding volatility.
Warrant subscription by Beryl's original promoter has not happened.
summary.management_tone: Confident and optimistic on margins, Beryl's turnaround and the US data-center opportunity, but evasive on acquisition size, price and EBITDA per barrel, and loose with numbers (several corrections during the call).
key_quotes: And this is another very important point to note here is this is without Beryl really contributing anything to the bottom line.

But the real contributor is high automation what we brought in our operations and an incentive system which is driving the people towards higher productivity is visible in the last at least 3 to 5 months.
So, these two are going to be a long term in nature. They are not one time.
And if the deal gets through, this combination can be really what makes us a complete civil engineering service provider.
So, we are now filling up that gap from Indians and local outside work. So, when you pay local outsiders, you don't make any money because their costs are the same.

adds.what: Proposed acquisition of US structural engineering firm (~15 engineers, half PEs/SEs)
Power/T&D design team ramp to 20 people (from ~10 billed in July)
Beryl Indian design team build-out to 15-20 people

growth.why: FY27 ex-Beryl revenue guided at Rs 240-250 crore (held) against ~Rs 61 crore already done in Q1, with FY28 indicative Rs 300-350 crore contingent on a structural acquisition; but the acquisition is not yet signed and the capacity adds are small headcount ramps, with MES cut to 50-60 people from 125-130 and Beryl still at break-even.
